adjudication_records.issue_text: PriorityLevel(new_status) in src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py (~line 298) blindly coerces DetectorPriorityLevel into PriorityLevel without validation that values match; raises ValueError at detection time if unmapped, and tests only cover the HIGH mapping

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` the diff adds `PriorityLevel(new_status)` when building an occurrence (`result, event_data = self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(..., PriorityLevel(new_status))`). `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel`, and this conversion assumes the enum values are compatible; if they ever diverge or include values not present in `PriorityLevel`, `Enum` construction will raise `ValueError` at runtime. The updated tests exercise the occurrence path only for `DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH` -> `PriorityLevel.HIGH` (via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event_data(..., PriorityLevel.HIGH)`), and do not cover other `DetectorPriorityLevel` values, so the potential edge case remains untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-group-key detection was removed in evaluate; results[result.group_key] = result silently overwrites duplicate keys with no error log or metric, allowing a misbehaving handler to silently drop results

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the handler contract from returning a list to returning a dict keyed by `DetectorGroupKey` (`DetectorHandler.evaluate` and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`). In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, it iterates `group_values.items()` where `group_values` is itself a dict (`get_group_key_values(...) -> dict[str, int]`), so duplicate group keys cannot occur from this path. The prior duplicate detection in `process_detectors` was only relevant when results were a list; with a dict return type, duplicates are not representable at the call site. The claim that `results[result.group_key] = result` will silently overwrite duplicates is not verifiable from this diff because `evaluate_group_key_value` constructs results with the same `group_key` it was called with, and the inputs are unique.

adjudication_records.issue_text: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts a value parameter but never uses it, so tests never verify detected value propagation to build_occurrence_and_event_data or the occurrence payload

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, group_key, value, new_status)` defines a `value` parameter but never references it when constructing the `IssueOccurrence` or `event_data` (it only uses `group_key`, `new_status`, and handler/detector fields). Meanwhile `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` now calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, ...)`, but the tests’ mock implementation (`MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data` -> `build_mock_occurrence_and_event`) cannot assert that the detected `value` is propagated/used in the occurrence payload. This is a concrete test-gap/coverage issue introduced by the new API, not a verifiable production defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test exercises the new else branch in evaluate_group_key_key_value combined with the OK-resolution path through process_detectors (produce_occurrence_to_kafka with StatusChangeMessage)

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add tests that exercise the new non-OK `else` branch in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` via `process_detectors`: `TestProcessDetectors.test_state_results` and `test_state_results_multi_group` patch `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` and assert it is called with an `IssueOccurrence` (i.e., the `else` branch calling `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). While it’s true there is no test that drives the OK-resolution (`StatusChangeMessage`) path through `process_detectors`/`produce_occurrence_to_kafka`, the finding’s claim that the new `else` branch is untested is contradicted by the added tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import builtins in src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py is used only to disambiguate builtins.type[GroupType], suggesting local shadowing of type; fragile given from __future__ import annotations is already present

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `import builtins` and uses it only in the return annotation `builtins.type[GroupType] | None` for `Detector.group_type`. There is no evidence in the diff that `type` is actually shadowed in this module scope (a model field named `self.type` doesn’t shadow the built-in name), and with `from __future__ import annotations` the annotation is not evaluated at runtime anyway. This is at most a minor style/readability nit (unnecessary `builtins` import), not a verifiable bug or important issue introduced by the change.
